architecture.mechanism: Second-order generalized integrator (SOGI) orthogonal-signal generation for the SRF-PLL supplies a frequency-adaptive, resonant-filtered estimate of the grid voltage, so during a sag the PLL's d/q reference does not oscillate and the inverter can remain synchronized and ride through.
architecture.intervention: Reflash the existing string inverters' firmware (no hardware, feeder, protection-curve, or storage change, keeping the certified LCL-filter grid-code envelope) to replace the park-transform PLL with a SOGI-QSG-based SRF-PLL (optionally SOGI-FLL for frequency adaptation) so the 0.6-pu, 200-ms utility-switching sags on the SCR 2.6 feeder no longer destabilize the reference frame and trigger the instantaneous undervoltage trip.
architecture.expected_effect: The SRF oscillation driving the instantaneous undervoltage trip during sag recovery is suppressed; the inverters stay locked through 200-ms, 0.6-pu sags, eliminating the roughly once-per-11-days trip cadence, while the existing LCL filter keeps injected-current THD within limits.
architecture.falsification_test: Flash one inverter string with the SOGI-QSG SRF-PLL and subject it to controlled 0.6-pu, 200-ms sags (or log naturally occurring events over a fixed window), comparing PLL q-axis error and undervoltage-trip counts against the baseline PLL on identical sags; the mechanism is falsified if trips are not eliminated or if current THD exceeds the certified limit.
